entries.reviewSummary: Defines department and director for chapter 375, and defines key terms for property insurance cancellation and nonrenewal sections.

headings.title: General chapter definitions
headings.reviewNote: Defines department and director as referring to the department and director of commerce and insurance.

headings.title: Definitions for policy cancellation and nonrenewal
headings.reviewNote: Defines insurer, nonpayment of premium, nonrenewal, policy, and renewal for sections 375.001 to 375.008.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes exclusive permissible grounds for property insurance policy cancellation and specifies exclusions.

headings.title: Authorized grounds for policy cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Limits effective cancellation to nonpayment of premium, fraud, conviction increasing hazard, or physical changes increasing risk.

headings.title: Inapplicability during initial sixty days
headings.reviewNote: Exempts policies in effect less than sixty days from statutory cancellation grounds unless the policy is a renewal.

headings.title: Inapplicability to policy nonrenewal
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section restrictions on cancellation do not apply to policy nonrenewal.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates property insurance cancellation notice timing, required statement of reasons, unequivocal effect of cancellation notices, permissive reinstatement, and nonrenewal exclusion.

headings.title: Thirty days advance notice of cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer to mail or deliver cancellation notice to named insured at least thirty days before the effective date.

headings.title: Ten days notice for nonpayment of premium
headings.reviewNote: Mandates ten days advance notice with specific bold statutory warning language for cancellation due to premium nonpayment.

headings.title: Statement of actual reason and FAIR plan notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires cancellation notice to state the insurer's actual reason clearly and specifically (excluding generalized terms) and notify the insured of possible Missouri FAIR plan eligibility.

headings.title: Notice as present and unequivocal act of cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that issuing a cancellation notice under subsection 1 or 2 constitutes a present and unequivocal act of cancelling the policy.

headings.title: Permissive reinstatement and post-notice communications
headings.reviewNote: Permits an insurer to reinstate a cancelled policy if the reason is remedied and send billing or reinstatement communications without invalidating the cancellation.

headings.title: Inapplicability of section to nonrenewal
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that section 375.003 does not apply to policy nonrenewal.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires thirty days advance notice and specific reasons for nonrenewal, preserves prior cancellation grounds upon renewal, and exempts affiliate or subsidiary policy transfers.

headings.title: Notice of nonrenewal and statement of reasons
headings.reviewNote: Requires at least 30 days advance notice of nonrenewal with specific reasons and FAIR plan eligibility notice, subject to exceptions for willingness to renew, nonpayment, insured refusal, or unpaid advance renewal premium.

headings.title: Renewal not a waiver of prior cancellation grounds
headings.reviewNote: Provides that renewing a policy does not constitute a waiver or estoppel regarding cancellation grounds existing before the renewal effective date.

headings.title: Exemption for affiliate or subsidiary policy transfers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts policy assignments or transfers to an affiliate or subsidiary effective upon expiration if notice is given, or at least 15 days advance notice with replacement policy access if coverage is not substantially equivalent.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines key regulatory terms for insurance producer licensing and oversight.

headings.title: Citation of Insurance Producers Act
headings.reviewNote: Provides that sections 375.012 to 375.146 may be cited as the Insurance Producers Act.

headings.title: Statutory definitions for producer licensing
headings.reviewNote: Defines nineteen terms including business entity, director, home state, insurer, insurance producer, limited lines, negotiate, sell, and solicit for sections 375.012 to 375.158.

headings.title: Statutory references to agents and brokers
headings.reviewNote: Deems all statutory references to insurance agent or insurance broker to mean insurance producer (text cites subsection 1, though definitions appear in subsection 2).

entries.reviewSummary: Requires insurance producer licensure, excludes insurers from producer licensing, enumerates exempt activities, and transitions pre-2003 licenses.

headings.title: License requirement for selling insurance
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits selling, soliciting, or negotiating insurance in Missouri without an insurance producer license for that line.

headings.title: Exemption of insurers from producer licensing
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that insurers are not required to obtain a producer license, excluding officers, directors, employees, subsidiaries, and affiliates from the term insurer.

headings.title: Persons and activities exempt from producer licensure
headings.reviewNote: Exempts eight categories from producer licensure, including non-commissioned administrative or claims staff, group plan administrators, employee benefit trustees, mass-media advertisers, multi-state commercial nonresidents, salaried risk advisors, and attorneys providing court bonds.

headings.title: Transition of licenses held on January 1, 2003
headings.reviewNote: Provides that licenses held on January 1, 2003 remain valid until renewal, when individual or business entity producer licenses are issued.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets application standards, age and character qualifications, business entity requirements, and verification powers for producers.

headings.title: Resident individual application and qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Requires resident individual applicants to file the uniform application and meet age 18, good-standing under section 375.141, $100 fee, and examination requirements.

headings.title: Business entity producer license requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires business entities acting as producers to submit the uniform business entity application, pay $100, designate a licensed responsible producer, and have no section 375.141 disqualifications.

headings.title: Director authority to require verification documents
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to require any documents reasonably necessary to verify information contained in an application.

headings.title: Business entity list of employed producers
headings.reviewNote: Requires a business entity application to list all employed or affiliated producers paid salary or commission for soliciting, negotiating, or procuring insurance.

headings.title: Twenty-working-day notice of entity changes or terminations
headings.reviewNote: Requires business entities to notify the director within 20 working days of application information changes or producer terminations without fee.

headings.title: Deemed approval after twenty-five working days
headings.reviewNote: Deems an application approved if the director takes no action within 25 working days of receipt, unless the applicant indicated a felony or moral turpitude conviction.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs producer licensing examinations, test administration, fee structures, retesting, and examination exemptions.

headings.title: Written examination requirement for resident applicants
headings.reviewNote: Requires resident individual applicants to pass written examination testing line-specific competence and insurance law.

headings.title: Outside administration of licensing examinations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to arrange for independent testing services to administer examinations and collect fees.

headings.title: Applicant examination fee payment
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to pay nonrefundable examination fee determined by director or outside testing provider.

headings.title: Reapplication after missed or failed examination
headings.reviewNote: Allows an applicant who fails to appear or fails to pass to reapply by remitting required fees and forms before rescheduling.

headings.title: Examination exemption for out-of-state licensees
headings.reviewNote: Exempts applicants currently licensed or applying within 90 days of good-standing cancellation in another state for the same lines, verifiable via NAIC producer database.

headings.title: Ninety-day resident application for relocating producers
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensed producers moving to Missouri to apply for a resident license within 90 days without examination for prior lines unless director regulations require otherwise.

headings.title: Examination exemption for limited lines applicants
headings.reviewNote: Exempts individuals applying for limited lines producer licenses from written examination.

entries.reviewSummary: Provides standards for nonresident producer licensure, reciprocity, change of address, and verification.

headings.title: Nonresident producer license qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Allows nonresident person to obtain producer license if licensed and in good standing in home state with reciprocity.

headings.title: Home state license verification methods
headings.reviewNote: Permits director to verify nonresident licensing status through NAIC producer database.

headings.title: Notice of change of residential address
headings.reviewNote: Requires nonresident producer moving to another state to file change of address within thirty days.

headings.title: Nonresident surplus lines producer reciprocity
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuing a nonresident surplus lines license to home-state surplus lines licensees under subsection 1 without otherwise amending chapter 384.

headings.title: Nonresident limited lines producer reciprocity
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuing a nonresident limited lines producer license granting the same scope of authority as the producer's home-state license.

headings.title: Reciprocal home-state continuing education satisfaction
headings.reviewNote: Deems compliance with home-state continuing education requirements to satisfy Missouri requirements (including chapter 384 surplus lines licensees) on a reciprocal basis.

headings.title: Equal nonresident fees and reciprocal requirement waiver
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits assessing higher fees solely for nonresidence and requires waiving non-subsection-1 application requirements for reciprocal home-state licensees.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs producer license issuance, qualification lines, biennial renewal, reinstatement grace periods, and address changes.

headings.title: Two-year producer license and lines of authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs issuance of a two-year producer license to qualified applicants across eight enumerated lines of insurance authority.

headings.title: Property license exemption for federal crop producers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts producers certified by the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation on September 28, 1995 from needing a property license to write federal crop insurance.

headings.title: Biennial $100 renewal fee and birth-date renewal
headings.reviewNote: Sets a $100 biennial renewal fee due on the producer's birth date, with the license continuing in effect until refused, revoked, or suspended under section 375.141.

headings.title: Individual producer license reinstatement within twelve months
headings.reviewNote: Permits individual producers to reinstate an expired license within 12 months without examination upon CE proof and payment of renewal fees plus a $25 monthly penalty.

headings.title: Business entity license reinstatement within twelve months
headings.reviewNote: Permits business entity producers to reinstate an expired license within 12 months by paying the renewal fee plus a $25 monthly penalty.

headings.title: Required contents of producer license
headings.reviewNote: Requires the license to contain the producer's name, address, identification number, issuance date, lines of authority, expiration date, and other director-required information.

headings.title: Thirty-day address notice and forfeiture penalty
headings.reviewNote: Requires producers to report an address change within 30 days and authorizes a forfeiture up to $10 per month for failing to timely report a legal name or address change.

headings.title: Contracting for ministerial licensing functions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to contract with nongovernmental entities, including the NAIC, to perform ministerial producer licensing functions and collect fees.

headings.title: Insurance law compliance for banks and trust companies
headings.reviewNote: Subjects banks and trust companies selling or issuing insurance products or services to Missouri insurance laws and department rules.

headings.title: Renewal waivers for military service or extenuating circumstances
headings.reviewNote: Allows licensed producers unable to comply with renewal procedures due to military service or extenuating circumstances such as long-term medical disability to request waiver of procedures and sanctions.

headings.title: Rulemaking to prorate birth-date biennial renewals
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes rules to implement the section, including prorating licensure periods for biennial birth-date renewals after January 1, 2022. Source note: original rolls cite nonexistent section 375.045, apparent typo for section 374.045.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes continuing education requirements for licensed producers, course approval, course provider fees, and waivers.

headings.title: Continuing education hours requirement for producers
headings.reviewNote: Requires non-exempt producers beginning January 1, 2008 to complete at least 16 hours of approved continuing education every two years covering Missouri law, products, department duties, and business ethics/suitability, with credit for general assembly members.

headings.title: Approved continuing education course categories
headings.reviewNote: Lists courses deemed to meet director standards subject to approval, including CLU/ChFC, LUTC, CIC, CPCU, IIA, approved designations, college courses, and insurer or association seminars.

headings.title: Continuing education credit for course instructors
headings.reviewNote: Grants persons teaching approved courses or lecturing at approved seminars the same classroom hours as students completing them.

headings.title: Carryforward of excess continuing education hours
headings.reviewNote: Permits excess hours accumulated during a two-year period to be carried forward to the immediately following two-year period.

headings.title: Good-cause extensions and individual hardship waivers
headings.reviewNote: Allows up to a one-calendar-year extension for good cause and individual waivers for serious injury or illness, extended active military duty, residence outside the United States, or age 70 or older.

headings.title: Producer and course provider completion certifications
headings.reviewNote: Requires producers to submit written completion certification and authorized providers to certify completions to the director within 30 working days.

headings.title: Exemptions for exam-exempt and limited lines producers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts natural persons holding exam-exempt licenses, limited lines licenses, or director-exempt restricted licenses from continuing education.

headings.title: Exemption for funeral-expense life insurance producers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts life producers contractually limited to life policies or annuities with initial face amounts of $20,000 or less designated for funeral or burial expenses.

headings.title: Rulemaking on course content and $50 approval fees
headings.reviewNote: Directs rulemaking utilizing the section 375.019 insurance advisory board for course content and sets a $50 per-course approval filing fee (waived for state and local producer groups) with one-year approval periods.

headings.title: Deposit of fees in insurance dedicated fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs transmittal of all section funds to the insurance dedicated fund and payment of section expenditures from legislative appropriations from that fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates insurer company registers of appointed producers, termination notices, confidentiality protections, and regulatory sharing.

headings.title: Maintenance of company register of appointed producers
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers to maintain an internal register of appointed producers authorized to transact business.

headings.title: Prohibition on acting without register listing
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits an insurance producer from acting on behalf of an insurer unless listed on the company register of appointed insurance producers.

headings.title: Inspection of register during business hours
headings.reviewNote: Directs that company register of appointed producers must be open to inspection by director during regular hours.

headings.title: Electronic maintenance of appointed producer register
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes insurer to maintain its company register of appointed producers in electronic format.

headings.title: Notice of termination for cause to director
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer to notify director within thirty days of terminating producer for reasons listed in section 375.141.

headings.title: Register update upon termination without cause
headings.reviewNote: Directs insurer terminating producer for other reasons to record termination date in register within thirty days.

headings.title: Duty to report subsequent discovered information
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer to promptly update director if it discovers additional reportable facts after initial termination notice.

headings.title: Confidentiality and immunity for termination reports
headings.reviewNote: Grants confidential and privileged status to termination notices and provides immunity for good faith reporting.

headings.title: Director use of termination materials in actions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to use termination reports and information in regulatory or legal proceedings.

headings.title: Privilege against testifying in civil actions
headings.reviewNote: Protects director and department staff from being subpoenaed or testifying in private civil actions concerning records.

headings.title: Information sharing with other regulatory authorities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes sharing confidential termination data with NAIC, law enforcement, and other regulatory agencies.

headings.title: Preservation of privilege upon disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sharing information with director or regulators does not constitute waiver of confidentiality privilege.

headings.title: Release of final adjudicated disciplinary actions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes reporting final adjudicated for-cause disciplinary actions to NAIC databases and clearinghouses.

headings.title: Public notice of license disciplinary action
headings.reviewNote: Requires director to provide public notice when suspending, revoking, or refusing producer license under section 375.141.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires demographic data collection, examination pass-rate reviews, and annual reports for life insurance producer examinations.

headings.title: Applicability to life insurance producer examinations
headings.reviewNote: Restricts section application exclusively to life insurance producer licensing examinations.

headings.title: Examination review upon low pass rate
headings.reviewNote: Requires review of licensing examination if first-time examinee overall pass rate falls below seventy percent.

headings.title: Collection of applicant demographic information
headings.reviewNote: Directs department to collect race, gender, and national origin demographic information from examinees.

headings.title: Annual report on demographic pass-rate disparity
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual report analyzing whether demographic examination pass-rate disparities exist.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes rules for demographic collection and reviews, conditioning authority on chapter 536 validity.

headings.title: Delivery of annual report to officials
headings.reviewNote: Requires director to deliver annual report to governor and legislative leadership by December first.

headings.title: Initial review period commencement date
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that initial twelve-month period for exam review begins on September 1, 2010.

headings.title: Initial report delivery deadline
headings.reviewNote: Sets December 1, 2011, as the delivery deadline for the department's initial exam review report.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes issuance of temporary producer licenses for up to ninety days and defines supervisory limitations.

headings.title: Issuance of temporary producer licenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to issue temporary ninety-day license upon producer death, disability, or active military deployment.

headings.title: Limitation and revocation of temporary authority
headings.reviewNote: Empowers director to limit authority, require licensed sponsor, and revoke temporary license to protect the public.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes continuing education credits for active participation in qualified professional insurance associations.

headings.title: Definitions for association continuing education credit
headings.reviewNote: Defines director and insurance producer for purposes of the section.

headings.title: Up to four hours credit for association participation
headings.reviewNote: Allows up to four biennial continuing education hours for active membership in a local, regional, state, or national professional insurance association, excluding classroom and ethics requirements, upon timely producer statement or association certification.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for association credits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to promulgate administrative rules implementing professional insurance association credit.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates ninety-day advance notice of producer contract termination and prohibits unauthorized transaction thereafter.

headings.title: Ninety days notice for contract termination
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurance company to give ninety days written notice prior to terminating independent agency contract.

headings.title: No new business during ninety-day notice period
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the independent insurance producer from writing or binding new business for the insurer during the 90-day notice period without specific written approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs one-year renewal rights for policies following termination of producer contract and commission payment.

headings.title: Policy renewal following contract termination
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer to renew existing policies through terminated producer for one year following contract termination.

headings.title: Commission payment on renewed policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers renewing contracts under this section to pay commissions to the terminated producer in the same amount and manner as under the terminated contract.

headings.title: Minimum duration of renewed insurance contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires renewals under this section to run for the greater of one year or one additional term of the original contract.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes director investigation and cancellation procedures for producer contract termination disputes, specifies solvency and misconduct exemptions, and provides severability.

headings.title: Investigation of producer contract terminations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director, on written complaint or own initiative, to determine violations of sections 375.031 to 375.037, notify parties by certified mail, prescribe a cancellation method, and allow judicial review under sections 536.100 to 536.140.

headings.title: Exemptions for insurer solvency, fraud, or misconduct
headings.reviewNote: Exempts cases where nonrenewal is necessary to preserve insurer solvency or protect insureds, or involving fraud, failure to remit premiums, or section 375.141 revocation or nonrenewal grounds.

headings.title: Severability of termination statutory provisions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that invalidity of any provision or application of sections 375.031 to 375.037 does not affect the remaining provisions or applications.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires written notice to producer before cancelling or nonrenewing an entire class of commercial risk.

headings.title: Notice to agent of class cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer to give sixty days advance notice to agent before cancelling or nonrenewing a commercial class.

headings.title: Thirty-day notice for reinsurance, loss, or department action
headings.reviewNote: Reduces required notice to at least 30 days when cancellation, termination, or withdrawal is due to reinsurance requirements, adverse loss experience, or department requirement.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires annual statement filing with the NAIC, grants data dissemination immunity, and provides suspension penalties.

headings.title: Applicability to authorized insurers and specified companies
headings.reviewNote: Applies the section to all authorized domestic, foreign, and alien insurers and companies organized and authorized under chapter 354, 377, 378, or 381.

headings.title: Annual March first NAIC statement filing
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing the annual statement convention blank (with signed jurat page, actuarial certification, and amendments) with the NAIC by March 1, deeming foreign insurers compliant under substantially similar domiciliary laws.

headings.title: Civil immunity for NAIC data collection and dissemination
headings.reviewNote: Grants NAIC members, committees, delegates, and staff civil immunity from libel, slander, or other actions for collecting, analyzing, and disseminating filing data absent actual malice or gross negligence.

headings.title: Certificate sanctions for failure to file statement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to suspend, revoke, or refuse to renew the certificate of authority of any insurer failing to file its annual statement when due or within an approved extension.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes producer trust and fiduciary accountability for moneys collected for insurers, applicants, and insureds without requiring separate bank accounts per payor.

headings.title: Fiduciary responsibility for collected premiums
headings.reviewNote: Deems insurance producer to be trustee of collected premium funds and requires fiduciary accountability.

headings.title: Fiduciary responsibility to applicants and insureds
headings.reviewNote: Holds insurance producers responsible in a trust or fiduciary capacity to applicants or insureds for any money collected or received on their behalf.

headings.title: No separate bank account required per payor
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that producers need not maintain a separate bank account for each payor's funds if the funds held are reasonably ascertainable from books and records.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs licensing, fee schedules, annual renewal, and commission authority for organizational credit business entities.

headings.title: Credit insurance producer license requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires credit business entities selling or soliciting credit insurance to obtain organizational credit license.

headings.title: Application form and employee list requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires organizational credit entity applicant to submit application and list of employees soliciting credit insurance.

headings.title: Listed employees deemed licensed credit producers
headings.reviewNote: Deems employees listed on the business entity's application to be licensed insurance producers for authorized credit lines under sections 375.014(1) and 375.141 without individual licenses.

headings.title: License issuance and annual renewal fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes annual license issuance and requires annual renewal fee of fifty dollars plus eighteen dollars per employee.

headings.title: Reinstatement of expired credit entity license
headings.reviewNote: Allows license reinstatement within twelve months upon paying renewal fee plus twenty-five dollar monthly penalty.

headings.title: Payment of commissions to credit entities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes insurance companies to pay commissions or remuneration to licensed organizational credit business entities.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for credit insurance licensing
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to promulgate rules implementing organizational credit business entity licensing.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes director participation in centralized producer license registry and adoption of uniform standards.

headings.title: Participation in centralized producer registry
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to participate in national centralized producer license registry with NAIC or affiliates.

headings.title: Adoption of uniform registry standards
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes adoption of uniform standards, procedures, and centralized fee collection for registry participation.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits paying or receiving insurance commissions without proper license, regulating deferred commissions and business entity assignments.

headings.title: Prohibition on commission payment to unlicensed persons
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers or producers from paying commissions to persons required to be licensed who lack license.

headings.title: Prohibition on receiving consideration without license
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits unlicensed persons from accepting commissions or compensation for selling or negotiating insurance.

headings.title: Payment of deferred renewal commissions
headings.reviewNote: Permits deferred or renewal commissions if individual was properly licensed at the time of the original transaction.

headings.title: Assignment of commissions to licensed entities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes commission payments to licensed business entities while barring payments to suspended or revoked licensees.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets short title, statutory purpose, scope exclusions, and disclaimer of private cause of action for claims settlement practices.

headings.title: Citation of unfair claims settlement act
headings.reviewNote: Cites sections 375.1000 to 375.1018 as the Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act.

headings.title: Purpose scope and private right exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Sets claim settlement standards, excludes workers compensation and boiler lines, and disclaims private causes of action.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes director administrative orders, level two violations, license revocations, and civil actions for claims practice violations.

headings.title: Administrative orders and penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative orders under section 374.046, classifies violations as level two, and allows license revocation.

headings.title: Civil actions for claims settlement violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to maintain civil actions under section 374.048 for improper claims settlement practices.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs written findings, cease and desist orders, monetary penalties, license sanctions, and order modifications.

headings.title: Cease and desist orders and monetary penalties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes written findings, cease and desist orders, civil penalties up to two hundred fifty thousand dollars, and license suspension.

headings.title: Modification of orders prior to judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Permits director to modify or set aside orders before the record is filed in Cole County circuit court.

headings.title: Reopening and modifying orders after review period
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to reopen and alter orders upon notice and hearing if conditions of fact or law have changed.

headings.title: Voluntary forfeiture agreements permitted
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sections 375.1000 to 375.1018 do not prohibit the director and a person from agreeing to a voluntary forfeiture with or without proceedings instituted.

entries.reviewSummary: Provides chapter 536 judicial review of final director orders in Cole County circuit court and preserves liability under other state laws.

headings.title: Judicial review of director cease and desist orders
headings.reviewNote: Provides for judicial review of director orders under chapter 536 in Cole County circuit court.

headings.title: Preservation of liability under other state laws
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that no director order under section 375.942 or court enforcement order relieves any affected person from liability under other Missouri laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes cumulative regulatory powers and administrative rulemaking authority under the claims practices act.

headings.title: Cumulative regulatory authority of director
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that statutory powers are in addition to any other powers of the director to enforce penalties.

headings.title: Promulgation of claims settlement rules
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to promulgate reasonable rules and regulations under chapter 536 to implement claims provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines applicability of annual audited financial report requirements and lists statutory exemptions.

headings.title: Applicability to insurers transacting business
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 375.1025 to 375.1062 to all insurers under section 375.1025, exempting those with under $1 million in Missouri direct premiums and under 1,000 nationwide policyholders unless the director finds compliance necessary or assumed reinsurance premiums reach $1 million.

headings.title: Exemption for foreign or alien insurers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts foreign or alien insurers filing audited reports under substantially similar statutes of other states.

headings.title: Foreign or alien internal control report exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts foreign or alien insurers from filing management's report of internal control over financial reporting if timely filed in another state with substantially similar requirements.

headings.title: Preservation of director examination authority
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sections 375.1025 to 375.1062 do not prohibit, preclude, or limit the director from ordering or conducting insurer examinations under other applicable law.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates annual audited financial report filing by June first, extension requests, and audit committee formation.

headings.title: Annual audited financial report filing deadline
headings.reviewNote: Requires all insurers to have annual audit by independent certified public accountant and file report by June first.

headings.title: Extension of audit report filing date
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to grant extension of filing date upon written request showing good cause.

headings.title: Corresponding extension for internal control report
headings.reviewNote: Grants a similar 30-day extension for filing management's report of internal control over financial reporting whenever a subsection 2 extension is granted.

headings.title: Audit committee of ultimate controlling person
headings.reviewNote: Permits audit committee of controlling entity to satisfy committee requirement at the election of governing body.

entries.reviewSummary: Specifies mandatory contents and comparative accounting format of annual audited financial reports.

headings.title: Financial condition scope and statutory accounting
headings.reviewNote: Requires the annual audited financial report to report financial condition, results of operation, cash flows, and capital and surplus changes conforming to domiciliary state statutory accounting practices.

headings.title: Required financial statements and reconciliation notes
headings.reviewNote: Lists six required report components: CPA report, balance sheet, statement of operations, cash flow statement, capital/surplus changes, and NAIC-required notes with annual-statement reconciliation. Source note: word 'and' before NAIC manual does not appear in original rolls.

headings.title: Annual-statement form and comparative two-year format
headings.reviewNote: Requires statements to mirror annual-statement language and groupings in comparative two-year format as of December 31, allowing omission of comparative data in the first filing year.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires accountant registration, awareness letter filing, and prompt notification of accountant dismissal or resignation.

headings.title: Registration of independent accountant with director
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer to register name and address of retained independent certified public accountant with director.

headings.title: Accountant representation letter to director
headings.reviewNote: Mandates accountant letter certifying awareness of statutory accounting standards and insurance department reporting.

headings.title: Notice of change of independent accountant
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer to notify director within five days of accountant dismissal or resignation and detail any disagreements.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes accountant qualification standards, audit partner rotation limits, nonaudit service prohibitions, and cooling-off rules.

headings.title: Independent certified public accountant qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Bars recognition of any CPA or firm not in good standing with the AICPA and licensing states (or chartered accountant for Canadian/British companies) or having an audit indemnification agreement.

headings.title: Recognition based on professional ethics standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires recognizing an independent CPA as qualified while conforming to AICPA and Missouri state board of accountancy professional ethics and conduct codes.

headings.title: Five-year lead partner rotation and hardship relief
headings.reviewNote: Limits lead or coordinating audit partners to five consecutive years with a five-year disqualification period, and allows requesting relief for unusual circumstances at least 30 days before year-end.

headings.title: Disapproval of unqualified accountants by director
headings.reviewNote: Empowers director to refuse to recognize accountants convicted of fraud or lacking independent professional standing.

headings.title: Hearing procedures on accountant disqualification
headings.reviewNote: Provides hearing under chapter 536 for accountants or insurers challenging director disqualification determinations.

headings.title: Mediation or arbitration agreements for audit disputes
headings.reviewNote: Permits qualified CPAs and insurers to agree to mediate or arbitrate audit disputes, operating at the statutory successor's option in sections 375.570 to 375.750 delinquency proceedings.

headings.title: Prohibited nonaudit services for audit clients
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates prohibited nonaudit services including bookkeeping, financial system design, internal audit, and appraisals.

headings.title: Exemption from nonaudit service prohibitions
headings.reviewNote: Allows small insurers with under one hundred million dollars in direct written premium to request relief.

headings.title: Nonaudit tax services permissible upon preapproval
headings.reviewNote: Allows accountant to perform nonaudit services including tax services if preapproved by insurer audit committee.

headings.title: Audit committee preapproval of audit services
headings.reviewNote: Requires audit committee to preapprove all auditing and permitted nonaudit services performed for insurer.

headings.title: Delegation of audit committee preapproval authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes audit committee to delegate preapproval authority to designated members who report to full committee.

headings.title: One-year employment cooling-off period for executives
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies accountant if former audit team member serves as insurer executive officer within one year preceding audit.

headings.title: Application of cooling-off period to partners
headings.reviewNote: Limits cooling-off rule to partners and senior managers and allows application for relief due to unusual circumstances.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates immediate written reporting of material financial misstatements and capital impairments, granting accountant immunity.

headings.title: Notice of material misstatement or impairment
headings.reviewNote: Requires accountant to notify insurer board within five days of misstatement or impairment, with notice to director.

headings.title: Immunity for good faith accountant notices
headings.reviewNote: Grants accountant civil immunity for reporting financial misstatements or surplus deficiencies in good faith.

headings.title: Accountant duties upon subsequently discovered facts
headings.reviewNote: Requires accountant becoming aware of new facts after report filing to follow AICPA professional standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires written communication of unremediated internal control material weaknesses and insurer remedial action descriptions.

headings.title: Accountant communication of unremediated weaknesses
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer to furnish director with accountant communication on internal control weaknesses within sixty days.

headings.title: Insurer description of remedial actions taken
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer to describe remedial actions taken or planned to correct internal control material weaknesses.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines accountant audit workpapers, regulates department examiner access, and establishes seven-year retention rules.

headings.title: Definition and scope of audit workpapers
headings.reviewNote: Defines workpapers as records of audit procedures, tests, and documentation supporting accountant opinion.

headings.title: Availability and seven-year retention of workpapers
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer to make audit workpapers available to examiners and mandates retention up to seven years.

headings.title: Photocopying authority and confidentiality of workpapers
headings.reviewNote: Permits department to photocopy workpapers and accords them statutory examination confidentiality.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs temporary audit hardship exemptions, compliance schedules for domestic and foreign insurers, and phase-in dates.

headings.title: Application and hearing for temporary hardship exemption
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to grant temporary hardship exemptions and provides administrative hearing upon denial.

headings.title: Compliance schedule for domestic insurers
headings.reviewNote: Establishes phase-in compliance deadlines for domestic insurers retaining or not retaining independent accountants.

headings.title: Compliance schedule for foreign insurers
headings.reviewNote: Requires foreign insurers to comply with audit provisions for year ending December 31, 1992, and thereafter.

headings.title: Effective date for partner rotation requirements
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that audit partner rotation requirements take effect for audits beginning January 1, 2010.

headings.title: Compliance schedule for audit committee provisions
headings.reviewNote: Sets transition timelines for insurers to establish qualifying audit committees under section 375.1053.

headings.title: Compliance schedule for internal control reporting
headings.reviewNote: Establishes effective date and compliance requirements for management reports on internal control.

headings.title: Effective date for internal audit function
headings.reviewNote: Sets January 1, 2019 as the effective date for section 375.1058 internal audit function requirements, with a one-year compliance period if an exempt insurer or group exceeds the threshold.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes audit committee responsibilities, independent member proportions, oversight duties, and hardship waivers.

headings.title: Exemption for foreign, alien, and SOX-compliant insurers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts licensed foreign or alien insurers, SOX-compliant entities, and direct or indirect wholly owned subsidiaries of SOX-compliant entities from this section.

headings.title: Audit committee appointment and direct reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires audit committee to be directly responsible for accountant appointment, compensation, and oversight.

headings.title: Audit committee oversight of internal audit function
headings.reviewNote: Makes the audit committee responsible for overseeing the internal audit function and granting suitable authority and resources when required by section 375.1058.

headings.title: Board membership requirement for committee members
headings.reviewNote: Requires each audit committee member to be a board member of the insurer or of an entity elected under subsection 7 and section 375.1025(4).

headings.title: Independence criteria and statutory board exception
headings.reviewNote: Bars independent committee members from accepting non-board compensatory fees or being affiliated persons, with an exception for law-mandated nonindependent board members who are not officers or employees.

headings.title: Temporary service after involuntary loss of independence
headings.reviewNote: Allows a member losing independence outside reasonable control, with notice to the state, to remain until the earlier of the next annual meeting or one year.

headings.title: Controlling person election to designate audit committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires the ultimate controlling person to provide timely written notice before the statutory audit report to designate the audit committee, remaining in effect until rescinded.

headings.title: Accountant reports on policies and alternative treatments
headings.reviewNote: Requires timely accountant reports to the audit committee on significant accounting policies, material alternative treatments, and material written communications, allowing aggregate holding-company reports if substantial differences are identified.

headings.title: Required proportion of independent committee members
headings.reviewNote: Sets independent-member minimums by prior-year direct and assumed premiums: none for $0-$300 million, a majority for $300-$500 million, and at least 75% for $500 million or more.

headings.title: Hardship waiver for insurers under $500 million
headings.reviewNote: Permits insurers with under $500 million in direct written and assumed premiums (excluding FCIC and Federal Flood) to apply for a hardship waiver and requires filing approval with annual statements and the NAIC.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits director and officer misrepresentations to accountants and improper influence over audits, establishing penalties.

headings.title: Prohibition against misleading independent accountant
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurer directors and officers from making materially false or misleading statements to accountant.

headings.title: Prohibition against coercing or manipulating audit
headings.reviewNote: Bars directors, officers, and employees from coercing or fraudulently influencing accountant conducting statutory audit.

headings.title: Actions constituting improper influence over audit
headings.reviewNote: Specifies prohibited acts that render financial statements misleading or prevent investigation of material facts.

headings.title: Level three violation penalty classification
headings.reviewNote: Classifies any violation of section 375.1054 as a level three violation under section 374.049.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs management report on internal control over financial reporting, premium thresholds, contents, and signatures.

headings.title: Management report on internal control filing
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurers with direct written premium exceeding five hundred million dollars to file management report.

headings.title: Director authority to require report for RBC or hazard
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to require management's internal control report regardless of premium threshold if the insurer is in any RBC level event or hazardous financial condition under section 375.539.

headings.title: Satisfaction using Sarbanes-Oxley Section 404 report
headings.reviewNote: Permits SOX-subject or SOX-compliant insurers or holding-company members to file a Section 404 report with a management addendum covering material statutory financial statement internal controls.

headings.title: Required contents and signatures of internal control report
headings.reviewNote: Specifies seven required report elements, including management responsibility, effectiveness assertion, evaluation approach, scope, disclosure of unremediated material weaknesses (barring an effectiveness conclusion), inherent limitations, and CEO/CFO signatures.

headings.title: Supporting documentation, framework discretion, and confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Requires documenting assertion bases for financial condition examinations, grants management framework discretion, and makes the report and supporting examination documentation confidential.

headings.title: Financial-reporting officers barred from audit committee
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any officer responsible for financial reporting from serving as a member of the audit committee.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes special audited financial report and letter requirements for Canadian and British branch insurers.

headings.title: Annual audited report definition for Canadian and British insurers
headings.reviewNote: Defines the annual audited financial report for Canadian and British insurers as the annual statement of total business filed with their supervision authority and audited by an independent chartered accountant.

headings.title: Accountant awareness letter for Canadian and British insurers
headings.reviewNote: Requires the section 375.1035(2) accountant letter to state awareness of section 375.1030 annual audited report requirements and affirm that the opinion conforms to those requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates internal audit function for large insurers, detailing premium thresholds, independence, and audit committee reporting.

headings.title: Premium-threshold exemptions from internal audit function
headings.reviewNote: Exempts an insurer with under $500 million in annual direct written and unaffiliated assumed premiums (excluding FCIC and Federal Flood) that belongs to a group totaling under $1 billion.

headings.title: Requirement to establish internal audit function
headings.reviewNote: Requires non-exempt insurers or groups to establish an internal audit function providing independent, objective assurance to the audit committee and management on governance, risk management, and internal controls.

headings.title: Organizational independence and board access
headings.reviewNote: Requires organizational independence without deferring ultimate audit judgment, appointment of an internal audit head with direct unrestricted board access, and permits dual-reporting relationships.

headings.title: Regular reporting by internal audit head to audit committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires at least annual reporting to the audit committee on the audit plan, factors impacting independence or effectiveness, material findings, and corrective actions.

headings.title: Holding-company or group-level compliance option
headings.reviewNote: Allows insurers in a holding company system or group to satisfy internal audit function requirements at the ultimate controlling parent, intermediate holding company, or individual legal entity level.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates actuarial certifications filed with annual statements, actuary qualifications, and director rulemaking authority.

headings.title: Actuarial certification for health services corporations
headings.reviewNote: Requires health services corporations under sections 354.010 to 354.380 to file an annual-statement certification by a member in good standing of the American Academy of Actuaries.

headings.title: Actuarial certification for life insurance companies
headings.reviewNote: Requires chapter 376 life insurance companies to file an annual-statement certification by an American Academy of Actuaries member, satisfied by a section 376.380(4) opinion complying with subsection 6.

headings.title: Actuarial certification for non-life insurers
headings.reviewNote: Requires chapter 379 insurance companies other than life companies to file an annual-statement certification by a member in good standing of the American Academy of Actuaries.

headings.title: NAIC life and health instruction conformity
headings.reviewNote: Requires health services corporation and life insurer certifications to conform to NAIC annual statement instructions for life and accident and health insurers, subject to subsection 6.

headings.title: NAIC property and casualty instruction conformity
headings.reviewNote: Requires non-life insurer certifications to conform to NAIC annual statement instructions for property and casualty insurers, subject to subsection 6.

headings.title: Mandatory American Academy of Actuaries membership
headings.reviewNote: Requires certifications under this section to be made by a member in good standing of the American Academy of Actuaries notwithstanding any NAIC annual statement instruction.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for actuarial certifications
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to adopt rules governing actuarial opinion format, scope, and reserve evaluation.

entries.reviewSummary: Imposes quantitative diversification caps on domestic insurer investments in medium and lower quality obligations.

headings.title: Aggregate limit on medium and lower quality investments
headings.reviewNote: Caps domestic insurer medium and lower quality obligations at 20% of admitted assets overall, with sublimits of 10% for SVO-rated 4-6, 3% for 5-6, and 1% for 6.

headings.title: Exception for prior binding purchase commitments
headings.reviewNote: Allows a domestic insurer to acquire obligations it previously committed to purchase if acquisition was permitted on the commitment date.

headings.title: Protective acquisitions of existing-issuer obligations
headings.reviewNote: Permits acquiring obligations of an institution in which the insurer already holds obligations to protect the prior investment, up to 0.5% of admitted assets.

headings.title: Board-adopted written investment and diversification plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board of directors of any domestic insurer investing in medium or lower quality obligations to adopt a written plan with quality and diversification standards.

headings.title: Nonrecognition of excess investments as admitted assets
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits recognizing investments exceeding the statutory limitations as assets of the insurer under section 379.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates domestic insurer investments in Canadian government obligations, corporate securities, and currency matching.

headings.title: Twenty-five percent admitted-assets cap on Canadian investments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits acquiring Canadian investments directly or through an investment subsidiary if aggregate Canadian investments would exceed 25% of admitted assets.

headings.title: Increased limit for insurers with Canadian obligations
headings.reviewNote: Increases the subsection 1 cap for insurers authorized in Canada or holding Canadian-currency contracts by the greater of Canadian legal investment requirements or 125% of Canadian-risk reserves and obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs risk retention group charter requirements, authorized liability lines, and annual financial statement filings.

headings.title: Liability-only charter and NAIC annual statement filing
headings.reviewNote: Requires risk retention groups to be chartered and licensed to write only liability insurance, comply with Missouri laws and section 375.1085, and file NAIC-format annual statements with the department and NAIC.

headings.title: Director approval of plan of operation and revisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting a plan of operation or feasibility study for director approval before offering insurance and submitting material revisions within 10 days before offering additional liability lines.

headings.title: Charter application summary disclosures forwarded to NAIC
headings.reviewNote: Requires charter applicants to submit summary information on initial members, organizers, capitalization, coverages, and target states, which the director must forward to the NAIC.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates foreign risk retention groups doing business in Missouri, tax liability, financial examinations, and policy notices.

headings.title: Foreign risk retention group qualification requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires foreign risk retention group to submit notice of operations and charter certificate before doing business.

headings.title: Submission of plan of operation and revisions
headings.reviewNote: Directs foreign risk retention group to submit plan of operation and revisions approved by its charter state.

headings.title: Designation of director as agent for process
headings.reviewNote: Requires foreign risk retention group to designate director as legal agent for service of process.

headings.title: Simultaneous filing of plan of operation revisions
headings.reviewNote: Requires foreign risk retention groups to submit plan of operation or feasibility study revisions to the director at the same time they are submitted to the chartering state.

headings.title: Ongoing financial, examination, and audit submissions
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting CPA-certified financial statements with actuarial loss-reserve opinions, certified examination reports, outside audit documents upon request, and continuing qualification information.

headings.title: Premium tax liability and agent recordkeeping
headings.reviewNote: Subjects risk retention groups and agents to premium taxation and detailed separate policy recordkeeping.

headings.title: Compliance with unfair claims settlement act
headings.reviewNote: Requires risk retention groups, their agents, and representatives to comply with sections 375.1000 to 375.1018.

headings.title: Financial examination by director upon inaction
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to examine financial condition if chartering state fails to initiate examination within sixty days.

headings.title: Mandatory ten-point policy warning notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires prominent statutory notice on policies warning that state insolvency guaranty funds are not available.

headings.title: Prohibited acts and ineligible insureds
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits selling insurance to nonmembers or operating group while in hazardous financial condition.

headings.title: Prohibition against insurance company ownership
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurance companies from owning risk retention group unless all members are insurance companies.

headings.title: Prohibition on unlawful or statutory coverage
headings.reviewNote: Bars risk retention group policies from providing coverage declared unlawful or prohibited by Missouri law.

headings.title: Compliance with dissolution and delinquency orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires compliance with lawful delinquency or dissolution orders commenced by director upon financial impairment.

headings.title: Sanctions and penalties for statutory noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Subjects noncompliant risk retention groups to fines and revocation of operating authority in Missouri.

headings.title: Compliance timeline for pre-existing groups
headings.reviewNote: Requires risk retention groups operating before August 28, 1991, to submit required notices within thirty days.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits risk retention group participation in guaranty funds and regulates purchasing group coverage and loss sharing.

headings.title: Guaranty fund participation and benefits barred
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits risk retention groups from joining or receiving benefits from Missouri insurance guaranty funds.

headings.title: No guaranty coverage for unauthorized insurers
headings.reviewNote: Excludes purchasing group risks from state guaranty funds when coverage is obtained from unauthorized insurers.

headings.title: Guaranty fund coverage for resident risks
headings.reviewNote: Provides that only resident Missouri risks are covered by guaranty funds when purchasing group uses authorized insurer.

headings.title: Participation in liability apportionment mechanisms
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to require risk retention groups to participate in joint underwriting loss apportionment.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires purchasing groups to furnish advance notice to director, report operational changes, and appoint agent for process.

headings.title: Advance notice of purchasing group operations
headings.reviewNote: Requires purchasing group to furnish notice to director identifying domicile, liability lines, and insurers.

headings.title: Ten days notice of changes in operations
headings.reviewNote: Mandates purchasing group notification to director within ten days of any changes in filed operational details.

headings.title: Designation of director for service of process
headings.reviewNote: Requires purchasing group to register and designate director as lawful agent for service of process.

headings.title: Supplemental qualification and location information
headings.reviewNote: Directs purchasing group to supply supplemental data required to verify qualification and appropriate tax treatment.

headings.title: Notice timeline for pre-existing purchasing groups
headings.reviewNote: Requires purchasing groups operating before August 28, 1991, to furnish statutory notice within thirty days.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates purchasing group procurement from authorized insurers, eligible surplus lines insurers, and risk retention groups.

headings.title: Authorized insurers for purchasing group procurement
headings.reviewNote: Restricts purchasing group coverage to authorized insurers or risk retention groups chartered in an appropriate state.

headings.title: Member notice of no guaranty fund protection
headings.reviewNote: Requires purchasing groups buying from nonadmitted insurers or risk retention groups to inform Missouri-risk members that coverage lacks state guaranty fund protection and may not be subject to all state insurance laws.

headings.title: Prohibition on group-wide deductibles or retentions
headings.reviewNote: Bars purchasing groups from buying insurance with a deductible or self-insured retention applicable to the group as a whole, while permitting individual-member deductibles or retentions.

headings.title: Application of group insurance aggregate-limit standards
headings.reviewNote: Subjects purchasing group insurance purchases to the same aggregate-limit standards applicable to all group insurance purchases.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires licensed agents or brokers for risk retention and purchasing groups, regulating nonresident licensure and disclosures.

headings.title: License requirement for placing group coverage
headings.reviewNote: Requires persons procuring or placing coverage for risk retention or purchasing groups to be licensed insurance producers.

headings.title: Agent, broker, and surplus lines licensing for purchasing groups
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensed agents or brokers for purchasing group coverage from authorized insurers or chartered risk retention groups, and surplus lines or excess line brokers for unauthorized insurers.

headings.title: Residency waiver for group surplus lines brokers
headings.reviewNote: Waives the Missouri residency requirement for surplus lines agents or brokers acting for a risk retention group or purchasing group under subsections 1 and 2.

headings.title: Producer duty to inform prospective insureds of notices
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensees placing business with risk retention groups or purchasing groups to inform prospective insureds of required notices (citing section 375.1085(7) and section 375.1095(3)).

entries.reviewSummary: Makes federal district court injunctions against financially impaired or hazardous risk retention groups enforceable in Missouri courts and authorizes director rulemaking.

headings.title: Enforceability of federal court injunctions in Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Makes any federal district court order enjoining a risk retention group from soliciting, selling, or operating due to hazardous financial condition or impairment enforceable in Missouri courts.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for risk retention groups
headings.reviewNote: Empowers director to establish reasonable rules and regulations under chapter 536 to implement sections.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs licensing of reinsurance intermediary brokers and managers, bond requirements, and attorney exemptions.

headings.title: Reinsurance intermediary broker licensing requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires reinsurance intermediary brokers representing Missouri insurers or operating in Missouri to hold license.

headings.title: Reinsurance intermediary manager licensing requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires reinsurance intermediary managers managing Missouri reinsurers or maintaining Missouri offices to hold license.

headings.title: Surety bond and errors omissions coverage
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to require reinsurance intermediary managers to maintain surety bond and errors and omissions policy.

headings.title: Reinsurance intermediary license issuance and nonresident process agent
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes issuing reinsurance intermediary licenses covering named members, officers, directors, and designated employees, and requires nonresident applicants to designate the director and a Missouri resident for service of process.

headings.title: Refusal to issue reinsurance intermediary license
headings.reviewNote: Empowers director to refuse license if applicant or controlling persons have demonstrated unfitness or committed disqualifying acts.

headings.title: Licensing exemption for licensed attorneys
headings.reviewNote: Exempts licensed attorneys acting in their professional legal capacity from reinsurance intermediary licensing.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates twenty-three-year medical malpractice and ten-year general reinsurance transaction record retention by brokers and guarantees insurer access.

headings.title: Twenty-three-year and ten-year broker record retention
headings.reviewNote: Requires reinsurance intermediary brokers to keep complete transaction records for at least 23 years after medical malpractice reinsurance expiration and at least 10 years after other reinsurance expiration.

headings.title: Insurer access to reinsurance broker records
headings.reviewNote: Directs that reinsurance intermediary broker records must be made accessible to insurer and available for inspection.

entries.reviewSummary: Restricts insurer engagement of reinsurance brokers, requiring licensing verification and annual financial condition statements.

headings.title: Restrictions on insurer use of brokers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits insurers from employing or retaining unlicensed reinsurance intermediary brokers.

headings.title: Restriction on dual employment with reinsurance broker
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits an insurer from employing an individual employed by a reinsurance intermediary broker with which it transacts business unless under common control subject to chapter 382.

headings.title: Annual financial condition statements of brokers
headings.reviewNote: Requires an insurer to annually obtain statements of the financial condition of each reinsurance intermediary broker with which it transacts business.

entries.reviewSummary: Restricts reinsurer engagement of reinsurance managers, mandating financial audits, loss reserves, and governance boundaries.

headings.title: Restrictions on reinsurer use of managers
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits reinsurers from retaining unlicensed reinsurance intermediary managers.

headings.title: Annual audited financial statement of manager
headings.reviewNote: Requires reinsurer to obtain annual audited financial report from each reinsurance manager it retains.

headings.title: Actuarial opinion on loss reserves established
headings.reviewNote: Mandates reinsurer to obtain independent actuarial opinion on loss reserves established by reinsurance manager.

headings.title: Officer authority for retrocessional contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires binding authority for retrocessions to remain with nonaffiliated officer of the reinsurer.

headings.title: Thirty days notice of manager termination
headings.reviewNote: Requires reinsurer to provide written notice to director within thirty days of terminating reinsurance manager contract.

headings.title: Prohibition against board appointments by manager
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits reinsurer from appointing officers, directors, or employees of reinsurance manager to its board.

entries.reviewSummary: Subjects reinsurance intermediaries to director examinations, records inspection, and reinsurer-level examination scope.

headings.title: Director examination of reinsurance intermediaries
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to examine reinsurance intermediaries with full access to books, bank accounts, and records.

headings.title: Examination of manager as reinsurer
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that a reinsurance intermediary manager may be examined by director as if it were the reinsurer.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes administrative sanctions, civil actions, mandatory restitution, and preserves third-party rights for intermediary violations.

headings.title: Administrative orders and license revocation penalties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative orders under section 374.046, level two violation penalties, and license revocation.

headings.title: Civil actions for reinsurance intermediary violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to maintain civil action under section 374.048 for violations of intermediary provisions.

headings.title: Restitution for losses caused by violation
headings.reviewNote: Requires reinsurance intermediary to make restitution to insurer, reinsurer, rehabilitator, or liquidator for net losses.

headings.title: Third-party rights preserved without expansion
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that intermediary sections do not limit or expand the rights of policyholders, claimants, or creditors.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets short title and defines broad applicability of the Insurers Supervision, Rehabilitation and Liquidation Act.

headings.title: Citation of insurers supervision and liquidation act
headings.reviewNote: Cites sections 375.1150 to 375.1246 as the Insurers Supervision, Rehabilitation and Liquidation Act.

headings.title: Applicability to insurers health plans and societies
headings.reviewNote: Applies proceedings to insurers, prepaid health plans, HMOs, fraternal benefit societies, and title insurers.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes exclusive director authority to commence insurer delinquency proceedings, asset situs, personal jurisdiction, and Cole County venue.

headings.title: Exclusive director authority for delinquency proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Bars commencement of insurer delinquency proceedings by anyone other than the director.

headings.title: Jurisdiction restricted to statutory delinquency act
headings.reviewNote: Denies court jurisdiction over insurer receivership or injunction actions except under sections 375.1150 to 375.1246.

headings.title: Situs and venue for domestic insurer assets
headings.reviewNote: Deems assets of domestic insurer to have situs within jurisdiction of supervising delinquency court.

headings.title: Personal jurisdiction over affiliated entities and obligors
headings.reviewNote: Extends personal jurisdiction over agents, reinsurers, officers, asset holders, and obligors of insurer in delinquency.

headings.title: Stay of proceedings for out-of-state forum
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes stay of Missouri action if court finds claim should in justice be tried in forum outside state.

headings.title: Mandatory venue in Cole County circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Places venue in circuit court of Cole County or county where insurer principal office was last located.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes receiver injunctions in Missouri and out-of-state courts to prevent asset waste and preserves counterparty rights under qualified financial contracts.

headings.title: Injunctions and restraining orders granted to receiver
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court to grant restraining orders preventing business operations, asset transfers, and lawsuits against insurer.

headings.title: Receiver authority to seek out-of-state injunctions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the receiver to apply to any court outside Missouri for the injunctive and restraining relief described in subsection 1.

headings.title: Preservation of contractual rights under financial agreements
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that delinquency proceedings do not stay contractual rights of counterparties to qualified financial contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates officer, employee, and affiliate cooperation with the receiver, prohibits obstruction, preserves existing legal rights, and governs official bonds.

headings.title: Duty to cooperate with receiver and director
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurer officers, directors, employees, and agents to cooperate with receiver in delinquency proceedings.

headings.title: Prohibition against obstructing delinquency proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits obstructing or interfering with receiver conduct of proceedings or concealing insurer records.

headings.title: Preservation of existing legal rights to resist
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not abridge existing legal rights, including the right to resist petitions for liquidation, delinquency proceedings, or orders.

headings.title: Official bond liability and additional court-ordered bonds
headings.reviewNote: Holds the director and deputies responsible on their official bonds and authorizes courts to require additional bonds paid from insurer assets as administration costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes prospective application of delinquency act, saving pending proceedings, and restricts insurer transactions during delinquency.

headings.title: Prospective application and saving clause for proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Applies act prospectively while allowing pending proceedings to continue under previous statutory provisions.

headings.title: Restrictions on insurer during delinquency proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits releasing an insurer from delinquency, restoring licenses or new business, or returning control or assets to shareholders or private management until guaranty associations and the department are repaid or a repayment plan is approved.

headings.title: Certified statements and exam reports as prima facie evidence
headings.reviewNote: Makes certified copies of insurer statements and department examination reports offered by the director prima facie evidence of facts regarding the insurer's condition and affairs.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes producer commissions and freedom of contract while prohibiting fees from applicants or insureds above policy premiums without a written compensation agreement.

headings.title: Authorized commission and brokerage payments to producers
headings.reviewNote: Permits insurers and producers to pay money, commissions, brokerage, or other value to duly licensed insurance producers for negotiating, placing, soliciting, or effecting insurance.

headings.title: Freedom of contract for producer commissions and fees
headings.reviewNote: Provides that chapter 375 does not restrict freedom of contract between insurers and producers regarding commission or fee amounts.

headings.title: Written agreement required for insured-paid compensation
headings.reviewNote: Bars producers from compensation from applicants or insureds beyond premium-deductible commissions without a written agreement specifying the compensation, while preserving premium recovery rights.

headings.title: Prohibition on charging above policy premium rate
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits producers from charging or receiving more than the policy's fixed premium rate from applicants or insureds unless authorized by a subsection 3 written agreement.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs administrative supervision of financially impaired insurers, confidentiality, supervisor powers, penalties, and immunity.

headings.title: Definitions of exceeded powers and consent
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'exceeded its powers' (nine enumerated conditions) and 'consent' for administrative supervision purposes.

headings.title: Grounds, registered-mail notice, and sixty-day cure period
headings.reviewNote: Sets five grounds for administrative supervision, requires registered-mail notice with cure requirements, provides 60 days (or director-designated period) to comply, and directs release when conditions cease.

headings.title: Confidentiality of supervision records and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Makes administrative supervision proceedings and records confidential, with exceptions for department staff, law-enforcement or agency disclosures, public-interest disclosures, and court-appointed receiverships.

headings.title: Supervisor appointment and fourteen restricted actions
headings.reviewNote: Designates the director or appointee as administrative supervisor and authorizes prohibiting 14 specified business, asset, policy, and compensation actions without prior approval.

headings.title: Thirty-day judicial review of supervision order
headings.reviewNote: Permits an insurer to seek section 536.150 judicial review within 30 days of a supervision order without staying the order's effect.

headings.title: Contesting supervisor actions and review of denial
headings.reviewNote: Allows an insurer to contest supervisor actions as not improving its condition and seek section 536.150 review of a written denial of reconsideration.

headings.title: Enforcement action for supervision order violation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to initiate an enforcement action under section 375.1161 against any person violating an active supervision order.

headings.title: Personal liability for losses from knowing order violations
headings.reviewNote: Imposes personal liability on persons knowingly violating valid supervision orders for resulting net-worth reductions or losses, recoverable by the director or supervisor under section 375.1161(1).

headings.title: Preservation of judicial delinquency proceeding authority
